findings: List.formPerm is the actual adjacent-transposition product associated with the displayed list. On a Nodup list it sends each listed element to the next listed element cyclically and fixes elements outside the list. The theorem's input is this concrete list construction, not an arbitrary permutation with a supplied splitting law.

The shared-endpoint concatenation and relabelling-conjugation lemmas are generic product identities. The head-conjugation lemma fixes every tail element because both alternative heads are absent, so it exchanges only the named head. These intermediate identities do not hide extra distinctness assumptions.

splitList_child_data derives the distinctness of a,b, all endpoint exclusions, the two child Nodup facts and disjoint child node sets from the single exact old-list Nodup premise. In particular neither child loses its incoming endpoint.

splitList_identity right-multiplies the original permutation by swap a b, so the swap applies first and exchanges the two old outgoing slots. Its result is exactly formPerm(a::B) times formPerm(b::A), preserving the source incoming-visit ordering instead of attaching a to A.

The proof factors at the shared endpoint, rotates the concrete prefix using its proved Nodup property, conjugates the two head cycles by the transposition, and commutes the final two factors using disjointness. It derives the entire permutation identity, including action outside the listed nodes.

Disjoint list node sets imply disjoint permutation supports through the one-way fixed-outside-list fact. The proof does not assert that a singleton list's permutation support equals its node set; List.formPerm[a] is the identity.

formPerm_mul_isCycleOn_left proves preservation and orbit transitivity on the explicit node-membership set. It compares integer powers using commutation and the second factor's pointwise fixing property. Canonical IsCycleOn allows the identity on a singleton set, so this proof retains one-node child cycles.

The two child IsCycleOn theorems and exact SameCycle membership equivalences identify the complete orbits of a and b with the sets of entries of(a::B) and(b::A). The forward implication uses invariance under integer powers and the reverse uses cycle transitivity. These statements remain valid when either or both of A,B are empty.

splitList_not_sameCycle uses disjointness of the two explicit child node sets to separate the incoming endpoints. When both arcs are empty, the switched permutation is the identity on the two distinct endpoints, correctly yielding their two separate singleton orbits.

The exact two-child conclusion concerns the displayed old-list domain. Elements elsewhere in an arbitrary ambient type are fixed by formPerm and can form additional singleton orbits. The packet makes no false claim that the entire arbitrary ambient type has only two components.
